closest.title: REST: Robust and Efficient Neural Networks for Sleep Monitoring in the Wild
closest.how_close: Closest methodological match. Trains an EEG sleep-staging CNN using PGD adversarial training and a spectral regularizer penalizing ||W^T W - I||_2, encouraging orthogonality and controlling layer Lipschitz constants. This substantially overlaps the proposed robustness mechanism, but uses a sleep-staging architecture rather than EEGNet and additionally targets compression.

closest.title: An efficient CNN-LSTM network with spectral normalization and label smoothing technologies for SSVEP frequency recognition
closest.how_close: Applies spectral normalization to an EEG-based BCI decoder and evaluates intra- and inter-subject classification. However, its CNN-LSTM architecture and focus on calibration efficiency and classification accuracy differ from Parseval-constrained EEGNet evaluated against adversarial attacks.

closest.title: Adversarial robustness benchmark for EEG-based brain–computer interfaces
closest.how_close: Matches the EEG-BCI adversarial-defense target and comparative evaluation setting. Evaluates nine defenses spanning robust training, adversarial pruning, input transformations, and ensembles; the available description does not establish the proposed Parseval or orthogonality-constrained EEGNet technique.

rationale: Very close work exists outside the bibliography, but I found no verified paper implementing the exact EEGNet–Parseval–adversarial-BCI combination. REST already applies an orthogonality-promoting spectral penalty and adversarial training to EEG CNNs, undermining the broad claim that this robustness mechanism is unexplored in EEG. Its sleep-staging task and architecture differ from the candidate's BCI decoding target. SSVEPNet separately establishes spectral normalization in BCI decoding, without the same adversarial-defense objective. These overlaps support a score of 3 rather than an exact-duplication finding. The candidate also conflates spectral normalization with Parseval constraints: bounding the largest singular value alone does not enforce a tight frame or approximate orthogonality.
